subject: Open vs Proprietary model assessment — recommended next steps & benchmarks
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@finserve.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Recap & proposed eval plan — open vs proprietary baseline

Liam / Ava — thanks again for the discovery earlier. Quick recap from our side and a pragmatic evaluation plan so we can converge on parity/acceptance criteria.

Summary of call
- Primary goal: determine whether open-source model stack can meet FinServe's accuracy and hallucination thresholds for customer support summarization and guidance.
- Baseline: you currently validate against FinCore-410B (proprietary) with internal nuance-handling rules.
- Constraints: latency targets (95th pct <= 350ms gen), data residency (US), and strict auditability for high-risk answers.

Recommended evaluation scope
1) Models to trial (initial):
   - Llama-3-13B-instruct (quantized candidate) — low-cost baseline for instruction tasks
   - Mistral-Instruct-7B-8K — high instruction-following quality with smaller footprint
   - RedFlag: include FinCore-410B run (your baseline) so we can measure delta both for quality and unit cost

2) Benchmarks & metrics (we'll run at scale):
   - Accuracy / intent-match (primary): target >= 92% to be considered parity for core flows
   - Factuality / hallucination rate (secondary): target <= 3% for answers flagged as facts
   - Safety/undesired-behavior triggers: binary pass/fail per policy set
   - Latency (95th pct) and per-token cost: report both so you can trade off

3) Prompt sets & evaluation harness
   - Please share a canonical sample set (representative 300–500 queries). We attached a starter CSV (FinServe_promptset_v1.csv) with 120 seed examples based on the call.
   - We'll expand the set with stratified sampling across complaint types, billing queries, and account escalation threads.

4) Acceptance gates and decisioning
   - If open model candidate meets accuracy >= 92% AND hallucination <= 3% AND 95th-pct latency within 1.2x of baseline, mark as "candidate to pilot".
   - If quality is within delta of baseline but cost is materially lower (>30% unit savings), propose a phased rollout with human-in-loop on high-risk segments.

5) Risks and mitigations
   - Regression concerns: we will run regression tests against your 2,000 labeled historical threads to detect quality regressions.
   - Auditability: we'll enable per-request logging + KV cache boundary markers for the pilot.

Next steps (proposed timeline)
- Week 0 (this week): get example data access + sign NDA subset + confirm required PII redaction rules.
- Week 1: dry-run benchmarks on the 120 seed prompt set and share a quick scoreboard.
- Week 2–3: scale to 1k examples, run A/B parity comparison vs FinCore-410B.
- Week 4: canary pilot (dedicated pool, 1% traffic) if gates pass.

Ask for you
- Share sample queries + a small labeled set (1–2k rows) or give read-only access to a temp S3 bucket.
- Confirm whether FinCore-410B outputs and scoring rules can be shared for exact delta calculations.

Attachments included: FinServe_promptset_v1.csv (seed prompts), finserve_parity_benchmarks.xlsx (blank template for results).

I'll roll this into a HubSpot task and a short technical doc in Drive. If this plan looks good I'll schedule a 30m follow-up to lock access and timelines.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

---

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@finserve.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Harris <ava.harris@finserve.com>, procurement@finserve.com
Date: 2027-04-11T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & proposed eval plan — open vs proprietary baseline

Thanks Diego — this is exactly the kind of plan we wanted. A few quick notes:
- We can provide the 1k historical threads (anonymized) by end of week if NDA subset is in place.
- FinCore-410B outputs can be shared internally; we'll need to redact anything with customer PII before sending.
- Procurement/ops are asking whether Redwood supports a short dedicated canary (we have strict SLAs).

On pricing: can you provide a rough cadence estimate for a 4-week pilot (1k evals + 30d canary at 1% traffic on a dedicated pool)? We'll decide internally whether to fund via PoC budget or push to procurement.

Happy to sync — Liam

---

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@finserve.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T13:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & proposed eval plan — open vs proprietary baseline

Liam — great, appreciate the quick turnaround. Short answers:
- NDA subset: we can accept a redacted bundle via S3 or secure Drive link; I added a Drive folder in related_links where we will drop interim reports.
- Dedicated canary: yes — Redwood Dedicated can be provisioned for a 30d canary. For a 1% traffic pilot we typically recommend a small reserved pool (equivalent to 1-2 A100 GPUs or a comparable multi-GPU virtual cluster depending on model choice); cost for 30 days including runs and storage is roughly $18k–$28k depending on exact model (Mistral vs Llama-3) and whether you use quantized variants.
- 4-week pilot estimate (ballpark):
   * Week 1–2 eval runs on 1k examples (parallel scoring): $3k–$6k compute + token costs
   * Week 3–4 canary (dedicated 30d pool): $18k–$28k reserved + operational support (one Solutions Engineer included)

I'll log a formal quote and a short SOW. Marcus — can you draft the PoC SOW template and include the audit logging requirements? Rachel — can you prepare the quick scoreboard template (parity vs FinCore) so we can populate after the dry run?

If this looks OK I'll schedule a 30m call tomorrow at 11am PT to confirm access and procurement next steps.

Thanks,
Diego

---

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: FinServe — immediate action items after discovery

Team — forwarding the thread. Action items: 
1) Marcus: draft the PoC SOW (include 30d dedicated canary pricing band shown above and optional human-in-loop plan). Target: first draft in 48 hours.
2) Rachel: build the parity scoreboard template (Accuracy, Hallucination rate, Latency p50/p95, Cost per 1k tokens, Safety flags). Attach to Drive link. Target: EOD tomorrow.
3) Neha: checklist for required compliance controls and audit logging for the canary (S3 logging, request-level traces, KMS key management). Bring up any blockers for Private deployment if they surface.

I'll own outreach for sample data access and coordinate NDA redaction guidance.

Diego
